warnings: Textual regulation codified manually; applicable_r_codes and operator are null for boolean/verification rules by design.

RCD (residual current device) requirements: NO provision found anywhere in Building Regulations 2012 (as at 17 Apr 2025) — RCD obligations arise under electricity safety legislation, not this instrument. Gap reported, no rule invented.

Photoelectric smoke alarm type: the term does not appear in this instrument; alarm type/location requirements are incorporated via the Building Code deemed-to-satisfy reference in r. 60(2)(a). Codified as such.

Barrier height 1200mm: appears in this instrument only as the modified boundary-barrier outside height (r. 15B cl. 2.2.4(b)(i)); general 1200mm fence heights live in AS 1926.1-2012 as referenced by the Building Code, not in the regulation text.

candidates.quote: Each owner and occupier of premises on which there is a private swimming pool containing water that is more than 300 mm deep must ensure that a pool barrier that restricts access to the pool and complies with the requirements of regulation 50A (and, if applicable, regulation 52) is installed or provided around the pool. Penalty for this subregulation: a fine of $5 000.
candidates.instrument_section: Part 8 — Existing buildings, Division 2 — Private swimming pools

condition_json.trigger: building (other than Class 10) within area bounded by pool barrier

candidates.quote: If all or part of a building (other than a Class 10 building) is within the area bounded by a pool barrier, that pool barrier or another pool barrier must restrict access to the pool from the building.
candidates.instrument_section: Part 8 — Existing buildings, Division 2 — Private swimming pools

condition_json.verification: barrier complies with Building Code pool barrier requirement in effect at/after permit application or construction commencement

candidates.quote: Subject to subregulations (3) and (4), a pool barrier must comply with a Building Code pool barrier requirement that was in effect — (a) if a building permit applies to the construction of the pool — at or after the time the application for a building permit to construct the pool was made; or (b) otherwise — at or after the time the construction of the pool commenced. Note for this subregulation: See also regulation 15B which modifies AS 1926.1-2012.
candidates.instrument_section: Part 8 — Existing buildings, Division 2 — Private swimming pools

condition_json.verification: performance solution used only if approved barrier solution

candidates.quote: For the purposes of subregulation (2), a performance solution cannot be used to comply with a Building Code pool barrier requirement unless the performance solution is an approved barrier solution.
candidates.instrument_section: Part 8 — Existing buildings, Division 2 — Private swimming pools

candidates.quote: If the pool is a pre-May 2016 private swimming pool, the pool barrier need not comply with subregulation (2) if — (a) it is in accordance with — (i) the requirements of AS 1926.1-1993; or (ii) approved alternative requirements; and (b) any wall comprising part of the pool barrier has no means of access to the pool through a building other than — (i) a window that is in accordance with the requirements of AS 1926.1-1993; or (ii) an approved door.
candidates.instrument_section: Part 8 — Existing buildings, Division 2 — Private swimming pools

condition_json.verification: AS 1926.1-1993 clauses 2.3, 2.6, 2.7 satisfied on either side of boundary fence

candidates.quote: For the purposes of subregulation (4)(a), a boundary fence of the premises that is part of the pool barrier is in accordance with the requirements of clauses 2.3, 2.6 and 2.7 of AS 1926.1-1993 if all those requirements are satisfied in relation to either side of the fence.
candidates.instrument_section: Part 8 — Existing buildings, Division 2 — Private swimming pools

condition_json.pool_era: installed before 5 November 2001 (or per plans submitted before that day)

candidates.quote: For the purposes of regulation 50(2), the immediate surrounds of a private swimming pool to which this regulation applies may include any part of the premises on which the pool is located. The pool barrier required by regulation 50(2) may include a wall that contains a door permitting access to the pool through a building if that door satisfies the requirements of AS 1926.1-1993.
candidates.instrument_section: Part 8 — Existing buildings, Division 2 — Private swimming pools

candidates.instrument_section: Part 8 — Existing buildings, Division 2 — Private swimming pools

candidates.quote: if the authorised person is not satisfied that regulation 50(2) is being complied with — on a day that is within 60 days after the day of the relevant inspection.

candidates.quote: A permit authority may approve a door for the purposes of regulation 50A(4)(b)(ii) if the door is in accordance with the requirements of AS 1926.l-1993 and — (a) in the opinion of the permit authority, a fence or barrier satisfying regulation 50A between the building and the private swimming pool would cause — (i) a significant problem of a structural nature; or (ii) a significant problem of any other nature, the cause of which is not within the control of the owner or occupier; or (b) the private swimming pool is totally enclosed by a building; or (c) in the opinion of the permit authority, a fence or barrier satisfying regulation 50A between the building and the private swimming pool would create a significant problem for a person with a disability who is resident at the premises and wishes to have access to the pool.
